The test the criterion names, which tells a gypsum rind on etched calcite from efflorescence on tooled stone, has not been made: the study of 2026 sampled efflorescence and loose material only, and found halite and no gypsum crust. Pitting is a normal result of salt crystallising in porous limestone.

claims.statement: The slab at the end of the Queen's Chamber south shaft is Tura limestone with copper pins, and Tura limestone has much more quartz than the local bedrock.
claims.criterion: Documentary check, not simulated: pass if quantitative mineralogy shows Tura limestone to be quartz-rich compared with Mokattam bedrock.
claims.basis: No evidence found: the quartz claim is attributed to no source, and the research files found no matched mineralogy of Tura limestone and Giza bedrock. The one compositional source opened, an author's summary of a study of 1984, pools six Tura and Mokattam quarry sites at 0.5 to 2.5 percent quartz and 96 to 99 percent calcite, which cannot show one richer than the other. That the slab is Tura limestone and its pins copper are judgements by eye, from polish and colour; neither was assayed.

claims.statement: A large void lies above the Grand Gallery, found by muon imaging.
claims.criterion: Geometric premise: pass if a published void of comparable size lies above the Gallery; its use as a heat exchanger is judged separately by the thermal criterion for the masonry between them (01 premise P5).
claims.basis: The muon paper of 2017 gives a void at least 30 m long, 0.64 of the Gallery's 46.7 m (0.64 to 0.86 over the 30 to 40 m carried for it), with its centre 14.7 m above the top of the Gallery roof (9.6 to 19.8 m) and its south end within 5 m of the pyramid's centre, over the Gallery in plan. Taking comparable as within a factor of 10 in the one dimension published, the order of magnitude that 01 allows (a judgement call), a published void of comparable size lies above the Gallery (it also holds within a factor of two). The section is inferred from the muon excess and not measured, and shape, inclination and the number of voids are open; the heat-exchanger use is judged separately.

claims.statement: Sodium chloride deposits cover the inside of the central pyramid's main chamber.
claims.criterion: Documentary check, not simulated: pass if a published analysis identifies sodium chloride on the walls of Khafre's burial chamber.
claims.basis: Partly supported: salt is documented in Khafre's burial chamber, but no analysis of it was found. Salt residue was cleaned from the chamber walls in 2003 to 2004, on a news report that was not re-checked, and Petrie, re-read at source, noted a good deal of crystallised salt inside the coffer. Sodium chloride is plausible, since halite is native to the bedrock the chamber is cut in, and for the same reason it would not show an acid process.

claims.statement: Chemical analysis shows catalyst material inside the Red Pyramid.
claims.criterion: Documentary check, not simulated: pass if a published analysis is produced; none is attributed in the transcripts.
claims.basis: No evidence found: no analysis is attributed in the transcripts, so there is no source to check, and the research files hold none. The research file lists the Red Pyramid's claimed function as not assessed, with no evidence found in its domain.

claims.statement: Cited article: the iron veins may be lightning vitrification or hydrothermal mineralisation, and the Sphinx stela records lightning striking the plateau.
claims.criterion: Documentary check, not simulated: pass if laboratory data show vitrified vein material and if the stela's lightning passage stands in a primary edition of the text.
claims.basis: Partly supported: the cited article does say both things, but neither condition of the criterion is met in full. The article, read in full, calls the features veins of vitrification, grants that iron-rich hydrothermal deposits may occur as well, and reports no sampling and no analysis, so there are no laboratory data for vitrified vein material; nobody has published that analysis. The lightning is in the Inventory Stela, an object of the 26th Dynasty: the translations attributed to Maspero and to Daressy have one great tree struck at the Place of the Sycamore, in an abraded passage whose reading is doubted, and Breasted's partial translation has no lightning at all. All three were seen as quoted on secondary pages, not in a primary edition. The passage records one strike, not how often lightning struck.

claims.statement: Vein samples show a hydrothermal origin, fulgurites and silica microspheres show high-voltage current, and many metals including rare earths are present.
claims.criterion: Documentary check, not simulated: pass if the sample analyses report fulgurite, glass or spherules, and metal levels above those of the local control sample.
claims.basis: No evidence found: the sample analyses were located and read in full, and they do not report what the claim says. The report, by an independent group and not peer-reviewed, covers 16 samples of iron-stained material from four of Khafre's boat pits and one control sample, not veins across the plateau, and it has no word for fulgurite, glass or sphere. Lanthanum, cerium and neodymium exceed the control in 3, 4 and 5 of the 16 samples, with medians about half the control, and thorium is below it in all 16; nickel, cobalt, vanadium, zinc and uranium are above it, as is usual for iron and manganese oxide fills. No fulgurite, vitrified rock or microspherule from Giza is documented in any source found.

claims.statement: Iron veins occur in the Osiris Shaft second level, in the Great Pyramid's subterranean shaft and in the central pyramid's bedrock chamber.
claims.criterion: Counts as wiring only if a four-point measurement along a vein against the adjacent rock gives a conductivity contrast high enough for the claimed link lengths; fail below 1e3 (07 section 4.2).
claims.basis: No evidence found: no four-point measurement along a Giza vein has been made, so the test the criterion names cannot be applied. Measured dry hematite spans the whole range: earthy red material is more resistive than the limestone, and the best specular sample gives a contrast of about 3e4 in 100 ohm m rock, above the criterion's fail line of 1e3 and below the 2.7e5 derived for a 100 m link. Observers describe the Giza fills as red, ochreous or dull black, the resistive end. Veins in the Osiris Shaft are reported from personal observation, and those in the two pyramids rest on the speaker's photographs. The research file expects a fail and says a measurement is needed.

claims.statement: The veins start under the two large pyramids and link features across the plateau.
claims.criterion: Pass only if the vein-to-host conductivity contrast reaches the value that a leakage length equal to the link length needs, about 2.7e5 for 100 m with a 0.03 m2 section; fail if it is below 1e3 (07 section 4.2).
claims.basis: A vein must conduct 2.7e+05 times better than the rock to carry current 100 m; the best measured specular hematite reaches 3.3e+04 times in 100 ohm m rock and 1.0e+06 times in the most resistive 3000 ohm m rock, earthy red hematite reaches 4.2e-02 times at most, and no Giza vein has been measured.

claims.statement: Boat pits by the Great Pyramid hold only sulfate compounds and those by the central pyramid only chloride compounds; channels lead into the pits.
claims.criterion: Pass if the pit walls show metres of retreat or thick gypsum crusts in the Khufu pits and none in the Khafre pits; tool-marked, uncorroded walls count against it (07 section 4.3).
claims.basis: Partly supported: chloride in Khafre's pits is supported, exclusivity is not, and the test the criterion names has not been made. The analyses behind the claim, an independent group's report that is not peer-reviewed and was read in full, cover Khafre's pits only: chlorine reaches 26.7 percent by weight, with gypsum named in almost every phase description, barite and celestine imaged and sulfur up to 5 percent, so chloride only is contradicted there. No analysis of Khufu's pits was found. No survey of the pit walls for retreat, gypsum crust or tool marks was found, which is what the criterion asks for. Khufu's two southern pits were found sealed over dismantled boats, on secondary accounts.

claims.statement: An underground shaft joins the Great Pyramid to the Sphinx enclosure, on the word of an unnamed ministry contact.
claims.criterion: Cannot be simulated; held as a documented constraint with no computed verdict (06, evidence that cannot be simulated).
claims.basis: No test exists: the criterion holds this as a documented constraint with no computed verdict. The basis is an unnamed acquaintance speaking on a tour. No survey, excavation report or publication describing such a tunnel was found, and the cavities known at the Sphinx are a few metres long, on secondary pages that were not opened.
